findings.title: Knowing becoming witness
findings.claim: The focus knowing can become compelled witness: an intense object is seen directly until knowledge is stabilized beyond doubt.
findings.mechanism: The exact HFT trace connects focus knowing to seeing in 102:6-7, blazing heat in جَحِيمَ, direct eye-presence in عَيْنَ, and settled certainty in ٱلْيَقِينِ; the later sensory sequence supplies the felt mode and force of the focus disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive knowing as an encounter that the senses and certainty make difficult to retreat from.
findings.containment: This remains an attributed contextual reading; the supplied alternative is that seeing simply follows knowing as a separate consequence. The unresolved heat branch receives no invented gloss.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exact at every supplied coordinate, but its witness synthesis is legacy-unbound attributed evidence and includes one unresolved branch.

All 11 assigned HFT records are visible and coordinate-complete, but their reader identity is legacy_unbound. Retained HFT findings therefore use attributed application mode, preserve live alternatives, and leave unresolved branch glosses and facets null.

The explicit external ayat 1:2-1:7 were reviewed only as a Phase 2 overlay. Their projected evidence supplied no candidate-specific carrier/trigger contact returning through 102:3, so no external overlay finding was retained; same-root omissions and cross-root mappings were not treated as activation.
The avian docket candidate was rejected as a topic-only cluster: its three branch refs and its two non-focus context refs are explicitly accounted for in the decision.
No uncandidate focus branch beyond the docket acquired a separate macro finding; the available world/created-being and male-hyena branches had no independent macro trigger in the supplied packet.
Connection rows supply exact target Arabic and relation notes but no target morphology; findings use them for relation assessment only and do not infer missing morphology.
